newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: SHELL SA OPPOSES NEW SOUTHERN AFRICAN REFINERIES.
newsitem.headline: SHELL SA OPPOSES NEW SOUTHERN AFRICAN REFINERIES.

text.p: The chief executive of Shell South Africa, John Drake, said on Friday he did not think new oil refineries for southern Africa were viable.

He told an economic conference in the Mozambican capital Maputo that demand for oil in Africa's most stable region was set to rise but that new refineries, often suggested for oil-producing Angola or well-positioned Mozambique, would not pay due to global competition and tight margins.
"We do not believe in these refineries in the short or the medium term," he said. "It's much cheaper to go for expansion of existing refineries."
South Africa has oil refineries near Durban, Cape Town and Johannesburg.
